question.name: CSEC Phy May 2022 Q4b(i) — State Archimedes' Principle
question.text:
State Archimedes' Principle by completing the statement below:

When an object is partially or fully [[1]] in a [[2]], it experiences an [[3]] (buoyant force) equal to the [[4]] of the [[2]] [[5]].
question.general_feedback:
Archimedes' Principle:

When an object is partially or fully immersed in a fluid, it experiences an upthrust (buoyant force) equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.

Formula: Upthrust = weight of fluid displaced = ρ × Vdisplaced × g

Applications:

  • Floating ships: upthrust = weight of ship → ship displaces its own weight of water
  • Submarines: change ballast to control depth
  • Hot air balloons: upthrust from air displaced
  • Measuring density using displacement method

Key word: Upthrust equals the weight (not volume) of fluid displaced. A common error is saying 'volume of fluid displaced'.

ddwtos.cloze_html: When an object is partially or fully [[1]] in a [[2]], it experiences an [[3]] equal to the [[4]] of the [[2]] [[5]].

groups.label: Archimedes' Principle — when a body is ___ in a fluid
groups.diagnostic_hint: IMMERSED (or submerged) — Archimedes' Principle applies when an object is fully or partially immersed in a fluid (liquid or gas).

groups.label: Archimedes' Principle — immersed in a ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: Immersed in a FLUID (liquid or gas). The principle applies to both. Most CSEC questions use liquid, but the principle is general.

groups.label: Archimedes' Principle — the ___ force equals...
groups.diagnostic_hint: The UPTHRUST (buoyant force) equals the weight of the displaced fluid. Upthrust acts upward on the immersed object.

groups.label: Archimedes' Principle — upthrust equals the ___ of displaced fluid
groups.diagnostic_hint: Upthrust = WEIGHT of the displaced fluid (not the volume or mass alone). Weight = mg, so upthrust = ρVg where ρ is fluid density, V is displaced volume, g is g.

groups.label: Archimedes' Principle — weight of ___ fluid
groups.diagnostic_hint: The "DISPLACED" fluid — the amount of fluid pushed aside by the immersed object. Its volume equals the volume of the submerged part of the object.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 19 tokens for 5 slots. Slot 1 (immersed/submerged): both accepted as equivalent. 'Floating' is wrong — floating is a consequence, not the condition. Slot 2 (fluid/liquid): fluid is the more accurate term (includes liquids and gases); liquid also accepted. Slot 3 (upthrust/buoyant force): both terms for the same force; 'downthrust' does not exist as a standard physics term; 'pressure' is not a force. Slot 4 (weight): the CRITICAL discriminator — 'volume' is the most common wrong answer. The upthrust equals the WEIGHT, not the volume, of fluid displaced. Slot 5 (displaced): 0 marks — this word is context and is essentially given in the stem.
